account.dossierIntro: Publix self-distributes almost everything its stores sell, out of a Florida-anchored DC network it owns and runs end to end. We mapped 11 of those distribution centers, from the Lakeland headquarters complex across the Southeast, holding 1,395 dock doors and room for about 2,550 trailers. Every one of the 11 sits behind a controlled truck gate, and seven run a staffed guard booth, so Publix already treats the yard as a checkpoint. YardFlow turns those manual gate stops into one orchestrated gate-to-dock flow across the whole network.
surprisingFindings: All 11 Publix DCs sit behind a controlled truck gate, 7 with a staffed guard booth. No retailer we have mapped gates its yards more tightly.
Three of the 11 DCs cluster at the Lakeland headquarters complex (grocery, frozen, produce), the dense core of a Florida-anchored network.
The 11 DCs hold 1,395 dock doors and 2,550 trailer spots, and only one touches rail, so nearly all of it moves by truck.

sites.name: Publix Distribution Campus Dacula GA (Atlanta)

steps.step: Arrive at gate (no guard, kiosk or call box)

sites.dossierExcerpt:
The supplied coordinates (33.990323, -83.927194) landed on the east dock edge of
a very large distribution complex — correct property, but not centered. Satellite
sweep (z14 -> z21) confirmed a major multi-building grocery distribution campus
matching the facility type. Web search corroborated: 445 Hurricane Trail is the
Publix-Atlanta Warehouse, a 24/7 receiving DC plus an on-site Atlanta Dairy
processing plant (AJC reported a 41,625 sq ft dairy production expansion). A
TruckersReport driver thread confirmed it as a large appointment-based DC with a
"huge bullpen for overnight parking." Locked center on the main DC building at
33.99080, -83.92950.

fieldNotes.truckGate: Single controlled truck entrance off the SW campus access road (Hurricane Trail spur off Sugarloaf Pkwy). Whole industrial property is chain-link fenced (confirmed in Street View along the south frontage). All truck traffic funnels through the SW access drive; rest of the perimeter is continuous fence + wooded buffer.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No standalone guard booth positively identified in satellite at the entrance drive; the entrance is set well back behind a tree buffer with no Street View coverage on the internal access road (ZERO_RESULTS at the gate). Marked false / remoteGs true as best evidence, but low confidence on the booth call.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Gate present but no visible guard shack -> implies kiosk/app/call-box check-in. Borderline with guardShack; flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.preGateStaging: Large overnight 'bullpen' parking and apron space outside/before the secured yard (confirmed by driver forum: 'huge bullpen for overnight parking').
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Wide internal truck artery and staging lanes between the drop yards and the dock faces.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long deep approach from the public road up the SW access drive into the yard; easily holds 3+ trucks.
fieldNotes.entryLanes/exitLanes: Estimated 2/2 from the wide SW access drive width; not separately barrier-counted, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide access drive apron and large paved yard provide ample room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 50+ band: both long faces of the main DC plus the dairy/processing and south warehouse buildings carry continuous dock-door banks; trailers backed in across all faces (z18/z19). Estimated ~140 total, low precision on exact count.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 50+ band: SW gravel drop yard plus west and north trailer lots hold well over 100 parked trailers (z19 truck-artery view shows dozens in angled rows in one lot alone).
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Distinct dock banks on physically separate building faces / separate buildings (main DC dry vs dairy/processing complex).
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus: main DC building + connected dairy/processing complex + south warehouse + maintenance/utility building = 4+ distinct structures.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale/weigh pad positively identified in available imagery; flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Inside dense suburban Atlanta metro fabric (Dacula/Lawrenceville, Gwinnett Co.) surrounded by subdivisions, parkway, and retail -> Urban.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated trailer-storage lots (SW gravel bullpen + west/north paved lots) separate from active dock staging.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~136 acres for the fenced industrial campus, derived from the traced perimeter polygon (excludes the rec fields/woods to the north).
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: Estimate ~360 across all drop yards and dock faces; honest overhead estimate, not exact.

sites.name: Publix Grocery Distribution Center McLeansville NC (Greensboro)

steps.step: Route to correct building / drop yard

sites.dossierExcerpt:
The supplied coordinates (36.083007, -79.664543) landed on the NW edge of a large
industrial campus. A zoom-15/16 sweep showed two very large distribution buildings
plus ancillary structures on a fenced parcel ringed by woods, fed by a single access
boulevard off Burlington Rd — consistent with the facility type and address. Web
research confirmed it: the Publix Greensboro-area distribution campus on the 5500
block of Burlington Rd (addresses 5544 / 5566), a ~$400M, ~1,000-job project. It was
built as an ~1M sq ft refrigerated warehouse and expanded with an ~1.2M sq ft dry
grocery warehouse (≈2.1–2.2M sq ft total), with a return center, fleet-maintenance
building, dispatch, and a security post on campus. Right building, locked center.

fieldNotes.truckGate: Whole campus is ringed by chain-link perimeter fence on a graded berm (confirmed in Street View along Burlington Rd frontage). A single divided access boulevard off Burlington Rd is the only way in; it is fenced on both sides and ends at a controlled checkpoint before the secure truck yard.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Publix newsroom/Gray/Procon project pages list a dedicated 'security post' on the campus. A small 1-2-vehicle-footprint structure with rooftop HVAC and a landscaped island sits at the throat between the employee lot, the entry boulevard and the secure truck yard (~36.0826,-79.6643). Satellite cannot resolve a booth window pattern at this resolution, so flagged uncertain, but the documented security post + the checkpoint structure strongly support a staffed guard shack.
fieldNotes.preGateStaging: Divided entry boulevard with wide aprons and the adjacent grassed pad gives ample room for trucks to stack outside the inner checkpoint.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved courtyard between the two main buildings and wide perimeter drives provide holding room inside the gate before backing to docks.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: The gate-to-dock approach is several hundred feet of wide internal drive; easily holds 3+ trucks.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Entry boulevard is divided into 2 inbound lanes; exact lane split at the inner checkpoint not resolvable from overhead, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.exitLanes: Outbound appears single-lane at the boulevard; uncertain.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide divided boulevard and large aprons leave unused paved width to add an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Two ~1M+ sq ft cross-dock buildings, each with long dock rows on multiple faces (north building south face into courtyard; south building both the courtyard face and the south-perimeter face). Counted bays band well into 50+ (estimate ~200+ total across the campus).
fieldNotes.dropArea: Dedicated marked trailer-parking lots east of the buildings and along the north drive are full of dropped trailers; far more than 50 stalls.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Dock banks sit on physically separate faces/buildings (refrigerated vs dry-grocery cross-docks plus a return center), so shipping and receiving run from distinct clusters.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town McLeansville, surrounded by woods, farmland and scattered houses outside the Greensboro metro fabric.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus has 5 distinct buildings: refrigerated warehouse, dry-grocery warehouse, fleet-maintenance building, return center/dispatch, and the security post (corroborated by Publix/Gray/Procon project pages).
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale/weigh pad identified in the truck path; flagged uncertain because the inner checkpoint area is partly obscured.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated trailer-storage lots on the east end and north drive, separate from active dock staging.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur enters the property; no tracks visible anywhere on or adjacent to the campus.
fieldNotes.yardMetrics: Counts are honest overhead estimates: dockDoorCount and trailer figures are approximate given the two very large multi-face cross-docks; siteAreaAcres derived from the traced perimeter ring (~99 ac).
